 ‘The Family Stone’ Sequel to Film Holiday Scenes in Rye
 City Council unanimously approved a request from Searchlight Pictures to film Dec. 5 and 9 at several locations around town. 
 By Miranda Ferrante 
 Published on 
 November 18, 2026 
 Downtown Rye during the holidays 
 More than two decades after “The Family Stone” hit theaters, the Stone family is returning to the big screen — and the City of Rye will provide a holiday backdrop for the upcoming sequel.
 The Rye City Council unanimously approved a request from Searchlight Pictures to film scenes for “The Families Stone” at several locations in the city on Saturday, Dec. 5, and Wednesday, Dec. 9, with filming activities scheduled between approximately 7 a.m. and 9 p.m.
 Deputy Mayor James Ward requested that the item be removed from the consent agenda to clarify several logistical details, including the production’s potential impact on residents and downtown businesses. The council briefly discussed those concerns with production representatives before approving the request.
 The sequel to the 2005 holiday film is moving forward, with several original cast members expected to return , including Sarah Jessica Parker, Rachel McAdams, Claire Danes, and Dermot Mulroney. The film will also pay tribute to the late Diane Keaton, who starred in the original.
 During the council’s meeting on Wednesday, location manager Jillian Stricker said the production team selected Rye for its small-town atmosphere and holiday setting. 
 Stricker said the scenes will feature family members gathering and interacting in public spaces, with the Village Green serving as a fictional town common.
 “We want there to be a beautiful backdrop of a small town for the holidays,” Stricker told the council. 
 The production will include holiday decorations, artificial snow and temporary filming equipment. Stricker said the crew has been coordinating with city officials, the police department and other departments to minimize disruptions.
 Council members raised questions about potential street closures, parking restrictions and the production’s impact on downtown businesses and holiday activities.
 Stricker said the production team has also been in contact with the Rye Chamber of Commerce to coordinate decorations and avoid interfering with existing holiday plans.
 The crew plans to bring in a Christmas tree and additional lighting for the Village Green, with discussions underway about whether some decorations could remain after filming. Stricker explained that the production requires incandescent lighting rather than LED lights, which can create flickering effects on camera.
 Council member Emily Baldwin raised concerns about parking, noting that the Rye Free Reading Room is scheduled to hold its Holiday Craft Fair on Saturday, Dec. 5 — one of the filming days. City Manager Brian Shea said arrangements were already underway to ensure parking would be available for the event.
 Rye has previously served as a filming location for several television productions, including the Apple TV+ series “Your Friends & Neighbors,” starring Jon Hamm and Amanda Peet. The show has filmed multiple seasons in Rye, including scenes for its third season earlier this year.
 The production is part of a growing film and television industry in Westchester County . According to a county economic report, film and television production generated $1.85 billion in economic activity in 2025, with industry employment increasing 86 percent and employee earnings reaching $535.6 million.
 “We love to see Westchester County in the movies or in TV,” County Executive Ken Jenkins said in September. “It’s not just for fun or a bragging point. It’s really big money.”
 Despite the logistical questions, council members expressed enthusiasm about bringing the production to Rye and welcomed the filmmakers to the city.
